correctness.rationale: For b>=1 and r>=0, a proved zero-gap minimization formula exactly characterizes the number of deletions needed to avoid 0 1^b 0. A counting dichotomy proves the lower bound b+2+2r+min(r,b-1); three exhaustive cases for the shortest witness prove sharpness, and inversion yields the n-profile. The executable independently compares automaton and gap methods on 163835 words, tests 75 extrema, 960 constructions and 1201 explicit deletion masks. Boundary cases r=0 and b=1 are included; finite computations are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The precise threshold is motivated by the 2026 forbidden-0110 argument used to separate insertion and deletion covering notions. The theorem resolves the entire infinite sandwich-pattern family, gives all fixed-length extremal deletion thresholds, and explains the switch from a cost of three to two added symbols per extra adversarial deletion at r=b-1. The structural zero-gap proof and explicit witnesses are not finite enumeration or a cosmetic substitution.
